title: Energy Assistance Payments and the Late Payment Charge on Electric Service Agreements — Training Notes
content:
These training notes answer questions about the hardship share applied to the late payment charge on an Electric Service Agreement when the agreement has received payments from an energy assistance agency.

**The rule.** The late payment charge is multiplied by a hardship share of one half (0.5) when the agreement received two or more payments from an energy assistance agency in the 12 calendar months before this charge, three quarters (0.75) when it received exactly one such payment, and one when it received none, and rounded to the cent. The hardship share acts on the amount obtained by applying the rate to the unpaid portion and rounding that product to the cent; the result is rounded to the cent again, and the schedule's late payment charge minimum is applied to that result.

**Which payments count?** Payments posted to the agreement through the energy assistance agency channel. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date, so an agency payment dated exactly 12 whole calendar months before the charge is no longer counted.

**What are the shares?**

| Energy assistance agency payments in the 12 calendar months before the charge | Hardship share |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 0.5 |
| exactly 1 | 0.75 |
| none | 1 (no reduction) |

**Does the minimum still apply after the share?** Yes. The minimum is applied to the shared amount, so a share can never take a charge below the schedule's minimum when any part of the bill is unpaid.

**Worked question (hypothetical figures).** The rate applied to a hypothetical unpaid portion of 232.00 USD at 1.5% gives 3.48. With exactly one agency payment in the 12 months the share is 0.75: 3.48 times 0.75 is 2.61. With two agency payments the share is 0.5: 3.48 times 0.5 is 1.74. If the minimum on that hypothetical schedule were 2.00 USD, the two-payment case would be raised to 2.00.
